notes: Passage explanations are educational paraphrases, not direct Qur'an translations. Verify translations and hadith numbering against a trusted edition before publication.

passages.title: Patience and Prayer
passages.body: When a person faces difficulty, the Qur’an teaches them to seek help through patience and prayer. Patience does not mean giving up or pretending that pain does not exist. It means remaining steady, avoiding harmful reactions, and continuing to do what is right while trusting Allah. Prayer helps a believer reconnect with Allah and remember that hardship is not faced alone.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does patience involve?
options: Giving up when life becomes difficult
Remaining steady and continuing to do what is right
Pretending that problems do not exist
Avoiding prayer until problems end
questions.explanation: Patience means staying firm and responding rightly during difficulty, while prayer strengthens reliance on Allah.

passages.title: Ease Alongside Hardship
passages.body: The Qur’an reminds believers that hardship is accompanied by ease. This promise does not mean every problem disappears immediately or that life will always be comfortable. It teaches hope: difficult periods are not the whole story. A believer should keep making responsible efforts, ask Allah for help, and avoid assuming that a painful moment will last forever.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the passage?
options: Every difficulty ends instantly
Hardship means a person has been abandoned
A difficult period should not destroy hope
Effort is unnecessary when life is hard
questions.explanation: The passage encourages hope and perseverance without promising that every difficulty ends immediately.

passages.title: The Value of Gratitude
passages.body: Gratitude is more than saying a few words when something good happens. It includes recognising blessings, using them responsibly, and not treating them as something we are automatically owed. A grateful person may thank Allah for health, family, knowledge, or even small opportunities. Gratitude can also change how someone treats others, because they become more aware of the good they receive.

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates gratitude as described?
options: Using blessings responsibly and acknowledging them
Assuming every blessing is deserved
Comparing every blessing with someone else’s
Thanking Allah only when receiving something expensive
questions.explanation: Gratitude includes recognition and responsible use of blessings, not just words.

passages.title: Speak in the Best Way
passages.body: Words can comfort people, solve misunderstandings, or cause lasting hurt. The Qur’an instructs believers to speak in a way that is best. This means choosing truthful and respectful words, especially when emotions are strong. It does not require agreeing with everything; a person can disagree while remaining fair and polite. Thoughtful speech protects relationships and reduces unnecessary conflict.

questions.question: What should a believer do when disagreeing with someone?
options: Use insulting words to prove a point
Stay respectful while explaining the disagreement
Spread the disagreement to embarrass the person
Avoid truth to keep everyone pleased
questions.explanation: Respectful disagreement allows a person to be honest without becoming insulting or unfair.

passages.title: The Importance of Intention
passages.body: An action is not judged only by how impressive it looks to other people. Its intention matters. Two people may perform the same outward action, yet their purposes can be very different. A sincere intention means doing something for the right reason rather than merely seeking praise or attention. This encourages believers to examine their motives before acting and to correct them when necessary.

questions.question: What does the passage say makes an intention sincere?
options: Doing something only when others are watching
Seeking praise as the main goal
Acting for the right reason rather than attention
Choosing actions only because they look impressive
questions.explanation: Sincerity concerns the purpose behind an action, not the attention it receives.

passages.title: Controlling Anger
passages.body: Anger is a human emotion, but it should not be allowed to control a person’s behaviour. The Qur’an praises those who restrain anger and pardon others. This does not mean accepting injustice or refusing to set boundaries. It means avoiding impulsive harm and choosing a response guided by wisdom. Sometimes the strongest response is to pause, calm down, and speak when the mind is clearer.

questions.question: What is the key difference between feeling anger and controlling it?
options: A person must never feel anger
A person can feel anger without acting harmfully
Anger always makes a person correct
Pardoning means accepting every kind of harm
questions.explanation: The passage distinguishes an emotion from the choice to act on it.

passages.title: Mercy Towards Others
passages.body: Mercy appears in everyday behaviour: being gentle with someone who is struggling, helping without humiliating them, and treating people with care. A person should not use power or knowledge to make others feel small. Mercy is not weakness; it can require patience and strength. When people show compassion, they help create a community where others feel safe asking for support.

questions.question: Which behaviour best reflects mercy?
options: Helping someone while humiliating them
Showing care and helping without making someone feel small
Ignoring people who need support
Using power to frighten others
questions.explanation: Mercy combines care with respect for another person’s dignity.

passages.title: Trust in Allah After Taking Action
passages.body: Trust in Allah is not an excuse to avoid planning or effort. The Qur’an describes consultation and then placing trust in Allah after a decision is made. A person should gather relevant information, seek good advice, make a responsible choice, and then rely on Allah regarding the outcome. This approach balances practical action with spiritual trust.

questions.question: Which sequence best matches the passage?
options: Ignore advice, avoid effort, and wait
Consult, make a responsible decision, then trust Allah
Make no plan because outcomes are unknown
Blame others before taking action
questions.explanation: The passage presents trust as something joined with consultation and responsible decision-making.

passages.title: Consistency in Good Deeds
passages.body: A small good action repeated regularly can shape a person’s character. Consistency builds habits and makes goodness part of daily life. People sometimes wait for a perfect moment or attempt too much at once, then become discouraged. A more sustainable approach is to begin with a manageable action and continue it sincerely. Gradual improvement can be more lasting than a short burst of effort.

questions.question: What approach does the passage recommend?
options: Doing a huge amount once and then stopping
Waiting until life is completely perfect
Starting with a manageable good action and continuing it
Avoiding small actions because they seem unimportant
questions.explanation: The passage highlights steady, sustainable effort rather than occasional extremes.

passages.title: Helping Others
passages.body: Helping another person can take many forms. It may involve sharing useful knowledge, giving practical assistance, listening carefully, or making a difficult task easier. Help should be offered with respect rather than as a way to show superiority. The Qur’an encourages cooperation in goodness and righteousness, reminding people that their abilities can benefit others.

questions.question: Which form of help best fits the passage?
options: Offering assistance respectfully for a good purpose
Helping only when praise is guaranteed
Making someone feel indebted and inferior
Supporting every action, even if it is harmful
questions.explanation: Good cooperation supports what is right and preserves the dignity of others.

passages.title: Choosing Forgiveness
passages.body: Forgiveness can free a person from carrying resentment, but it does not require pretending that wrongdoing was acceptable. A person may forgive while also setting healthy boundaries or seeking justice through appropriate means. The Qur’an praises patience and forgiveness, especially when these choices are made with strength and wisdom rather than fear.

questions.question: What does forgiveness NOT require?
options: Letting go of resentment where possible
Pretending that wrongdoing was acceptable
Choosing a wise response
Setting boundaries when necessary
questions.explanation: Forgiveness does not mean approving harm or removing every boundary.

passages.title: Honesty Even When It Is Difficult
passages.body: Honesty is tested when telling the truth may be uncomfortable or may bring a personal disadvantage. The Qur’an commands believers to stand firmly for justice, even when the matter concerns themselves or close relatives. This teaches that truth should not change according to personal benefit. Honest conduct builds trust and helps people make fair decisions.

questions.question: When is honesty especially tested?
options: When the truth is easy and popular
When truth may be uncomfortable or disadvantageous
Only when someone is being watched
When it benefits a close friend
questions.explanation: The passage explains that justice and truth must be maintained even when personally difficult.

passages.title: Avoiding Unfair Suspicion
passages.body: People often make assumptions after hearing incomplete information. The Qur’an warns against excessive suspicion, spying, and backbiting. Before judging someone, a person should consider whether the information is reliable and whether the conclusion is fair. Respecting privacy and avoiding gossip protect relationships and prevent harm caused by rumours.

questions.question: What should someone do before judging another person?
options: Treat every rumour as fact
Spread private information to get opinions
Check whether information is reliable and avoid unfair assumptions
Search for private details without permission
questions.explanation: The passage advises against suspicion, spying, and gossip, and encourages fairness.

passages.title: Human Dignity and Equality
passages.body: People come from different families, communities, and backgrounds. The Qur’an explains that humanity was created as peoples and tribes so that people may know one another. Differences should not become reasons for arrogance or contempt. True honour is connected with righteousness, not wealth, family name, appearance, or social status.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should not determine a person’s worth?
options: Righteous conduct
A person’s social status or family background
Good character
Respectful behaviour
questions.explanation: The passage rejects pride based on lineage or status and points to righteousness.

passages.title: Keeping Trusts and Promises
passages.body: Trust is built when people fulfil their responsibilities and do not misuse what has been placed in their care. A promise should not be made carelessly, and an entrusted item or duty should be handled honestly. The Qur’an warns believers not to betray trusts knowingly. Reliability matters in family life, study, work, and community relationships.

questions.question: What behaviour shows that someone respects a trust?
options: Ignoring a responsibility when it becomes inconvenient
Using entrusted property for personal benefit without permission
Handling responsibilities honestly and carefully
Making promises without intending to fulfil them
questions.explanation: Respecting a trust means fulfilling responsibilities and not betraying what is entrusted.

passages.title: Kindness to Parents
passages.body: The Qur’an connects worship of Allah with showing excellent treatment to parents. This includes speaking respectfully, avoiding harshness, and showing care as they grow older. Kindness does not mean obeying a request to do something sinful or harmful; respect can remain even when a person must disagree. The passage encourages gratitude for the care parents have given.

questions.question: How can someone disagree with a parent while following the passage?
options: By insulting them
By speaking harshly to end the discussion
By remaining respectful while not following a harmful or sinful request
By refusing to show any care
questions.explanation: Respect and kindness remain important, while obedience is not required for wrongdoing.

passages.title: Avoiding Wastefulness
passages.body: Resources such as food, water, money, and time should be used thoughtfully. Wastefulness can happen when people take more than they need or use resources without considering their value. The Qur’an teaches moderation and condemns extravagance. Being careful with resources does not mean refusing to enjoy lawful blessings; it means using them responsibly.

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates moderation?
options: Taking more food than can be eaten and throwing it away
Using resources thoughtfully and avoiding excess
Spending money only to impress others
Wasting time because it has no value
questions.explanation: Moderation means avoiding excess and using resources responsibly.

passages.title: Seeking Beneficial Knowledge
passages.body: Knowledge helps people understand the world, make sound decisions, and recognise their responsibilities. The Qur’an teaches believers to ask Allah for an increase in knowledge. Seeking knowledge should be accompanied by humility: learning more should make a person more careful, not arrogant. Useful knowledge is strengthened when it is applied with good character.

questions.question: What attitude should accompany the search for knowledge?
options: Arrogance toward people who know less
Humility and a willingness to apply learning well
Refusing to ask questions
Using knowledge only to show superiority
questions.explanation: The passage connects learning with humility and responsible action.

passages.title: Remembering Allah
passages.body: The Qur’an describes hearts finding reassurance through the remembrance of Allah. Remembrance can include prayer, supplication, reciting Qur’an, and reflecting on Allah’s guidance. It does not mean a believer will never feel sadness or worry. Rather, remembrance can give direction and comfort while a person continues to address real-life responsibilities.

questions.question: What does remembrance offer according to the passage?
options: A guarantee that no sadness will ever occur
Comfort and direction while facing responsibilities
A reason to ignore every practical problem
A way to avoid all effort
questions.explanation: Remembrance supports the heart but does not remove the need to handle responsibilities.

passages.title: Good Treatment of Neighbours
passages.body: A good community is built through consideration for people nearby. The Qur’an instructs believers to show kindness to neighbours, relatives, travellers, and others in need. Small actions matter: keeping noise reasonable, offering help, and avoiding behaviour that causes unnecessary trouble. Respect should not depend only on whether a neighbour can return a favour.

questions.question: Which action shows consideration for neighbours?
options: Making avoidable noise late at night
Helping only if a reward is promised
Avoiding unnecessary disturbance and offering help when needed
Ignoring a neighbour in difficulty
questions.explanation: Kindness to neighbours is shown through practical care and avoiding harm.

passages.title: Fairness With Everyone
passages.body: Fairness should not depend on whether we like someone. The Qur’an tells believers to stand firmly for justice and not let dislike of a group lead them away from fairness. This principle is important during disagreements, competitions, and decision-making. A fair person considers evidence and gives others their due, even when emotions make that difficult.

questions.question: What should guide a fair decision about someone we dislike?
options: Personal dislike
Rumours from friends
Evidence and justice
A desire to take revenge
questions.explanation: Justice must not be abandoned because of personal dislike.

passages.title: Returning to Allah
passages.body: People make mistakes, but a mistake does not have to become the end of their story. The Qur’an tells those who have wronged themselves not to despair of Allah’s mercy. Sincere repentance involves recognising the wrong, feeling regret, stopping the harmful action, and making a genuine effort not to return to it. When another person’s rights were harmed, those rights must also be addressed.

questions.question: What is an important part of sincere repentance?
options: Hiding the mistake while continuing it
Recognising the wrong and making a genuine effort to stop
Assuming mercy means actions do not matter
Blaming everyone else
questions.explanation: Repentance includes turning away from wrongdoing and trying to correct it.

passages.title: Choosing Good Company
passages.body: The people around us can influence our habits, language, and decisions. The Qur’an encourages believers to remain with truthful people. Good company does not mean looking down on others; it means choosing close influences that encourage honesty, responsibility, and remembrance of what is right. A person should also try to be a positive influence in return.

questions.question: What is the main reason to choose good company?
options: To feel superior to other people
To be influenced toward truthful and responsible behaviour
To avoid helping anyone outside the group
To copy every action friends take
questions.explanation: Good company encourages positive conduct, while arrogance and blind imitation are not the goal.

passages.title: Gentleness in Interaction
passages.body: A gentle approach can make advice easier to hear and disagreements easier to resolve. The Qur’an describes the Prophet’s gentleness and notes that harshness can drive people away. Gentleness does not mean hiding important truths; it means communicating them with wisdom, patience, and consideration for the listener.

questions.question: How should important advice be communicated?
options: With humiliation so the listener remembers it
With wisdom and consideration
By spreading the person’s mistake publicly
By avoiding truth completely
questions.explanation: Gentleness supports effective advice without requiring dishonesty.

passages.title: Verify Information
passages.body: Information can be incomplete, mistaken, or deliberately misleading. The Qur’an instructs believers to verify reports so that they do not harm people through ignorance and later regret what they have done. Before forwarding a message, a person should check its source and context. This is especially important when a claim could damage someone’s reputation.

questions.question: What should someone do before forwarding a serious claim?
options: Forward it quickly before it disappears
Check its source and context
Assume it is true because it is popular
Add more details to make it convincing
questions.explanation: Verification helps prevent harm caused by false or incomplete reports.

passages.title: Walking With Humility
passages.body: Humility means recognising that a person is not better than others simply because of wealth, knowledge, strength, or status. The Qur’an warns against walking arrogantly and looking down on people. A humble person can still be confident and work toward goals, but does not need to belittle anyone to feel important.

questions.question: Which behaviour reflects humility?
options: Mocking someone with fewer resources
Listening respectfully and avoiding arrogance
Showing off achievements to embarrass others
Treating status as proof of superiority
questions.explanation: Humility is compatible with confidence but rejects arrogance and contempt.

passages.title: Speaking With Moderation
passages.body: The Qur’an advises moderation in one’s voice and describes the unpleasantness of shouting without need. This guidance encourages people to communicate calmly rather than using volume to dominate a conversation. A quiet voice is not always the answer in every situation, but ordinary discussion should show self-control and respect.

questions.question: What does moderation in speech encourage?
options: Shouting to control every discussion
Speaking calmly instead of raising the voice unnecessarily
Never speaking in public
Using a loud voice to appear confident
questions.explanation: The passage encourages calm communication and discourages unnecessary shouting.

passages.title: The Value of Consultation
passages.body: Important decisions can become stronger when people seek advice and listen to different perspectives. The Qur’an praises believers whose affairs are conducted through consultation. Consultation does not mean that every person must agree or that responsibility disappears. It helps decision-makers consider information they may have missed before making a thoughtful choice.

questions.question: What is the purpose of consultation?
options: To avoid making any decision
To hear perspectives and make a more thoughtful decision
To transfer all responsibility to others
To ensure everyone always agrees
questions.explanation: Consultation helps improve decisions while responsibility remains with the decision-maker.

passages.title: Responding to Harm With What Is Better
passages.body: The Qur’an teaches that good and evil are not equal and encourages responding with what is better. This can help turn hostility into a calmer relationship. It does not mean allowing ongoing abuse or placing oneself in danger. It means avoiding revenge-driven behaviour and choosing a constructive response when it is safe and wise to do so.

questions.question: What qualification is important when responding constructively to harm?
options: A person must remain in danger
Constructive responses should be chosen when safe and wise
Harm should always be repaid with greater harm
Boundaries are never allowed
questions.explanation: The passage encourages better conduct while recognising that safety and wise boundaries matter.

passages.title: Do Not Despair
passages.body: A person may feel overwhelmed after making mistakes or facing repeated setbacks. The Qur’an warns people not to despair of Allah’s mercy. Hope should encourage action: seek forgiveness, correct what can be corrected, and take the next responsible step. Despair can make a person stop trying, while hope can help them return to what is good.

questions.question: How should hope affect a person after a mistake?
options: Make them ignore the mistake
Encourage them to seek forgiveness and take a better next step
Convince them that change is impossible
Make them blame others
questions.explanation: Hope in mercy should lead to repentance and constructive action, not denial.

passages.title: Giving From What We Value
passages.body: Giving is meaningful when it comes from genuine care rather than a desire to impress others. The Qur’an encourages spending from good things people have earned. Charity can support people in need and remind the giver that possessions are a responsibility. The value of giving is not measured only by the amount; sincerity and the benefit to others matter.

questions.question: What makes giving meaningful in this passage?
options: Giving only to gain public praise
Offering something beneficial with sincere care
Giving unusable items to clear storage
Helping only people who can repay it
questions.explanation: The passage highlights sincerity and giving from what is good and useful.

passages.title: Care for Orphans and the Vulnerable
passages.body: The Qur’an repeatedly warns against mistreating vulnerable people, including orphans. A child without parental care may need protection, fairness, and practical support. Helping such a person should never become an opportunity to take advantage of them. A responsible community safeguards their rights and treats them with dignity.

questions.question: Which action protects an orphan’s dignity?
options: Using their belongings without permission
Taking advantage of their limited support
Safeguarding their rights and treating them fairly
Ignoring their needs because they are not relatives
questions.explanation: The passage emphasises protecting vulnerable people and their rights.

passages.title: Honouring Agreements
passages.body: Agreements help people cooperate with clear expectations. The Qur’an instructs believers to fulfil contracts and commitments. Before accepting an agreement, a person should understand what is being promised and whether it can be fulfilled. Once a fair commitment is made, it should not be abandoned simply because a more convenient option appears.

questions.question: What should someone do after making a fair commitment?
options: Abandon it whenever something easier appears
Try to fulfil it responsibly
Pretend it was never made
Change its terms secretly
questions.explanation: Honouring agreements means taking commitments seriously and fulfilling them responsibly.

passages.title: Protecting People’s Reputation
passages.body: Backbiting can damage trust even when the speaker thinks the conversation is harmless. The Qur’an uses a strong warning against backbiting and asks believers not to speak about others in ways that violate their dignity. If a genuine concern must be raised, it should be addressed responsibly and only with those who need to know, rather than becoming entertainment or gossip.

questions.question: What is a responsible alternative to gossip?
options: Discussing private faults for entertainment
Sharing rumours in a group chat
Addressing a genuine concern privately and appropriately
Inventing details to make a story interesting
questions.explanation: The passage distinguishes responsible action from gossip that harms reputations.

passages.title: Using Time Well
passages.body: Time is a limited trust. The Qur’an draws attention to the loss people face when they waste their lives, while describing those who succeed through faith, good deeds, truth, and patience. This encourages a balanced routine: make time for responsibilities, worship, learning, rest, and helping others. Good time management is not about being busy every minute; it is about using time purposefully.

questions.question: Which routine best reflects purposeful use of time?
options: Filling every hour with activity and never resting
Balancing responsibilities, worship, learning, and rest
Delaying every responsibility until the last moment
Spending all free time comparing oneself with others
questions.explanation: Purposeful time use includes important duties and rest rather than constant busyness.

passages.title: Even Small Good Deeds Matter
passages.body: The Qur’an teaches that whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. This reminds people not to dismiss small choices. A kind message, an honest answer, or a quiet act of help may seem minor, but small actions contribute to a person’s character and carry moral significance.

questions.question: What lesson follows from the example of an atom’s weight?
options: Only large actions matter
Small actions have no value
Even small good and bad actions matter
Good actions matter only when others notice
questions.explanation: The passage teaches accountability for even very small actions.

passages.title: Working on the Self
passages.body: Personal growth requires noticing harmful habits and making an effort to improve them. The Qur’an connects success with purifying the soul and failure with corrupting it. Self-improvement is not about claiming to be perfect or judging everyone else. It involves honest self-reflection, repentance, and repeated effort to develop better character.

questions.question: What is a healthy approach to self-improvement?
options: Pretending to have no weaknesses
Judging others instead of reflecting
Recognising harmful habits and working to improve
Expecting change without effort
questions.explanation: Self-improvement begins with honest reflection and sustained effort.

passages.title: Faith and Good Actions
passages.body: The Qur’an often connects faith with righteous deeds. This pairing reminds believers that faith should influence daily behaviour. It should appear in honesty, kindness, responsibility, and fairness, not only in claims or words. Good actions do not make a person flawless, but they show an effort to live according to what they believe.

questions.question: What does the connection between faith and good deeds emphasise?
options: Belief should influence everyday conduct
Words alone make actions unnecessary
A person who makes a mistake can never improve
Good behaviour is only for public display
questions.explanation: Faith is meant to shape a person’s choices and conduct.

passages.title: Being Just in Testimony
passages.body: A truthful witness should not change their account to protect a friend, family member, or personal interest. The Qur’an instructs believers to uphold justice even when testimony is against themselves or close relatives. This principle protects people from decisions based on favouritism and reminds us that truth matters more than convenience.

questions.question: What should a witness do if the truth may disadvantage a relative?
options: Change the facts to protect the relative
Remain truthful and uphold justice
Stay silent only to avoid discomfort
Invent a compromise story
questions.explanation: Justice requires truthful testimony even when the outcome is personally difficult.

passages.title: Giving Without Hurting
passages.body: Giving loses part of its kindness when it is followed by reminders that humiliate the receiver. The Qur’an teaches that kind words and forgiveness are better than charity followed by hurt. A person should protect the dignity of someone receiving help and avoid using generosity as a way to control them.

questions.question: What should a giver avoid after helping someone?
options: Respecting the receiver’s privacy
Speaking kindly
Reminding them of the help to humiliate or control them
Offering help sincerely
questions.explanation: Charity should not be followed by hurtful reminders or humiliation.

passages.title: Cooperating in Goodness
passages.body: People often achieve more when they work together, but cooperation needs a clear moral direction. The Qur’an encourages helping one another in righteousness and mindfulness of Allah, not in sin or aggression. Before joining a group activity, a person should consider what the activity supports and whether it harms anyone.

questions.question: When is cooperation encouraged?
options: When it supports goodness and righteousness
Whenever a group asks, regardless of the action
When it helps people harm someone
Only when personal benefit is guaranteed
questions.explanation: Cooperation is encouraged for good purposes, not wrongdoing or aggression.

passages.title: Respecting Differences
passages.body: People may disagree about ideas, customs, and preferences. Respect does not require pretending that all opinions are identical. It requires avoiding mockery, insults, and unfair assumptions. The Qur’an warns people not to ridicule one another, because those being mocked may be better in the sight of Allah. This encourages humility when interacting with people who are different.

questions.question: What should someone avoid when meeting people with different views?
options: Listening carefully
Mocking or insulting them
Discussing differences respectfully
Checking their own assumptions
questions.explanation: The passage warns against ridicule and encourages humility and respect.

passages.title: Maintaining Prayer
passages.body: Prayer is a central act of worship and a regular opportunity to remember Allah. The Qur’an instructs believers to establish prayer and be mindful of it. A steady routine can help someone protect prayer times amid study, work, and other responsibilities. If a person has been inconsistent, they should return to prayer rather than allowing discouragement to keep them away.

questions.question: What should a person do after becoming inconsistent in prayer?
options: Give up because the routine was broken
Return to prayer and work on a steadier routine
Wait until life becomes completely easy
Assume prayer is no longer important
questions.explanation: The passage encourages returning to worship and building consistency.

passages.title: Avoiding Arrogance
passages.body: Arrogance can make a person reject advice, look down on others, or believe that success makes them superior. The Qur’an warns against turning away from people in pride and walking arrogantly. A person can take pride in sincere effort while remaining grateful and respectful. Success should increase responsibility, not contempt.

questions.question: Which response to success avoids arrogance?
options: Believing others are beneath you
Rejecting all advice
Remaining grateful and respectful
Using achievement to embarrass others
questions.explanation: Gratitude and respect prevent achievement from becoming a reason for pride.

passages.title: Hope With Effort
passages.body: Hope is not simply waiting for a better future. It can motivate a person to take practical steps while asking Allah for help. The Qur’an teaches that Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves. This encourages personal responsibility: identify what needs improvement and begin with actions within your control.

questions.question: What does the passage connect with positive change?
options: Waiting without changing anything
Taking responsible steps to improve oneself
Blaming circumstances for every choice
Expecting others to do all the work
questions.explanation: The passage connects change with personal responsibility and effort.

passages.title: Learning From Prophetic Example
passages.body: The Qur’an presents the Messenger of Allah as an excellent example for those who hope in Allah and the Last Day. Learning from this example involves more than knowing historical details. It includes reflecting on qualities such as trustworthiness, patience, mercy, and commitment to what is right, then trying to practise those qualities in daily life.

questions.question: How should a believer benefit from the Prophetic example?
options: By learning details but ignoring character
By reflecting on good qualities and practising them
By using history only to win arguments
By assuming good character is unnecessary
questions.explanation: The passage focuses on applying admirable qualities in everyday conduct.

passages.title: Good Character in Daily Life
passages.body: Good character is visible in ordinary moments: keeping a promise, listening without interrupting, admitting a mistake, and treating people fairly. The Qur’an instructs believers to speak upright words. Good character is not limited to public situations; it matters when no one is watching too. Consistent behaviour builds trust over time.

questions.question: Which action is an example of good character?
options: Admitting a mistake and correcting it
Keeping a promise only when watched
Interrupting others to dominate
Treating people well only when they can offer a reward
questions.explanation: Good character is demonstrated through honesty, responsibility, and respect in everyday situations.

passages.title: Remembering the Hereafter
passages.body: The Qur’an reminds people that worldly life includes temporary attractions and that lasting success is connected with what a person sends forward through faith and good actions. This does not mean neglecting family, study, or lawful work. Rather, it encourages people to keep their priorities balanced and remember that choices have consequences beyond immediate pleasure.

questions.question: What practical lesson comes from remembering the Hereafter?
options: Ignore all worldly responsibilities
Balance daily responsibilities with awareness of lasting accountability
Pursue pleasure without considering consequences
Assume good intentions make actions irrelevant
questions.explanation: Remembering accountability helps a person make balanced and responsible choices.

passages.title: Giving Quietly
passages.body: Giving in private can protect the receiver’s dignity and help the giver avoid seeking attention. The Qur’an praises charity and explains that concealing it when giving to the poor can be better. Public giving may sometimes encourage others, but the intention and the dignity of those receiving help must remain central.

questions.question: Why can private charity be especially valuable?
options: It can protect dignity and reduce the desire for praise
It guarantees that nobody else will ever give
It makes the amount more important than the intention
It allows the giver to control the receiver
questions.explanation: Private charity can preserve dignity and help guard sincerity.

passages.title: Responding to Kindness
passages.body: When someone helps us, acknowledging their effort is part of good manners. Gratitude encourages healthy relationships and reminds people that they depend on one another. The Qur’an teaches people to respond to a greeting with one that is better or at least return it. This illustrates the wider value of responding to kindness with goodness.

questions.question: What response reflects the lesson in the passage?
options: Ignoring kindness as unimportant
Responding to kindness with appreciation and goodness
Expecting help without ever acknowledging it
Using another person’s kindness to exploit them
